::: {#exr-radius}
## Radius of convergence

Consider the power series
$$
  \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{x^k}{2^k}
$$
with the partial sums $s_n(x)$ for $x = 1$ and $x = 3$

::: {.lm-sheet}
```{r}
n <- 0:8
s <- function(x) cumsum((x / 2)^n)
kable(data.frame(n = n, "x = 1" = s(1), "x = 3" = s(3), check.names = FALSE), digits = 4)
```
:::

Determine the radius of convergence and explain the table.
:::

## Part 2: In R

Download the [work files](07-power-series-exercises.zip) and unzip them into your project folder.

::: {#exr-taylor}
## Taylor polynomials of the exponential function

The power series of $e^x$ converges for all $x$. Its partial sums are the Taylor polynomials
$$
  T_n(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{x^k}{k!}.
$$

### Implementation

Implement the function `taylor_exp(x, n)`, which returns $T_n(x)$.

### Errors

Compute the errors of $T_1(1), \ldots, T_{15}(1)$. How does the error fall?
:::
